briefing.summary: Descend about 800 m to the Lost City Hydrothermal Field, a cluster of towering white carbonate chimneys on the Atlantis Massif. Find and scan the Poseidon tower, then survey the smaller chimneys and the real terrain around the field.
facts: Lost City runs on serpentinization: seawater reacting with mantle rock. Its warm, alkaline fluid emerges clear, leaving pale carbonate towers.
Poseidon stands about 60 m tall. Carbonate samples elsewhere in the field record activity reaching back about 120,000 years.
The towers stand on a sloping terrace of the Atlantis Massif, around 750–900 m deep.
Microbial communities use hydrogen and methane from the vent fluid as sources of energy.
hazards: Fragile mineral formations: the carbonate spires are delicate and slow-growing. Keep a respectful distance.
Sunlight fades with depth; use your lights to read the deeper terrain.
